 US News Agregar Clarín en X Will GTA 6 have a 60 FPS or 40 FPS mode? Rockstar explains why it's locked at 30 FPS on PS5 and Xbox
 If you were hoping for a performance mode in Grand Theft Auto 6, you will need to adjust your expectations. Rockstar Games has officially confirmed that the highly anticipated title is locked at 30 FPS across all current-generation consoles, including the powerful PS5 Pro. 
 With no 60 FPS or 40 FPS modes available at launch, developers explain that the sheer complexity, AI density, and ray-traced visuals of Vice City are simply too demanding for current console hardware.
 What time is GTA 6 coming out? Playable unlock times by region and how to preload on PS5 and Xbox 
 Rockstar Games has officially confirmed that the highly anticipated title is locked at 30 FPS across all current-generation consoles, including the powerful PS5 Pro NEWSROOM CLARIN For players who prioritize smooth framerates over graphical fidelity, the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 comes with a significant technical caveat. 
 Rockstar Games has officially confirmed that the game will not feature a 60 FPS Performance mode, nor will it offer a 40 FPS Balanced mode for 120Hz displays. Instead, the game targets a strict 30 FPS cap across all current-generation consoles: PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S.
 While many developers in this console generation offer a choice between a 60 FPS Performance mode and a 30 FPS Quality mode, Rockstar has opted for a single, locked presentation. 
 Here is a breakdown of the technical limitations preventing a 60 FPS mode and why Rockstar chose to prioritize the complex simulation of Vice City.
 Why is there no 60 FPS or 40 FPS mode in GTA 6?
 The decision to lock the game at 30 FPS comes down to the immense strain that GTA 6's dense open world places on both the CPU (Central Processing Unit) and GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) .
 Vice City is an incredibly alive, complex ecosystem filled with overlapping systems, massive amounts of traffic, dozens of planes in the air, and multiple NPCs (non-playable characters) filling every frame.
 According to Jonathon Ashcroft , Rockstar’s Senior Vice President of Technology, the "complexity of simulating and rendering our world" makes higher framerates impossible on current hardware.
 "The complexity of simulating and rendering our world, with so many systems that need to weave together dynamically, requires us to carefully balance how we spend every millisecond of both the central processor and the graphics processor ," Ashcroft explained to TechRadar Gaming . "It's a tremendous amount of work to do and only 33ms [milliseconds] to do it. The frame rate we've chosen gives us the right balance of presentation, simulation, and gameplay ."
 Why can't the PS5 Pro run GTA 6 at 60 FPS?
 Many gamers hoped that Sony’s recently released mid-generation upgrade, the PlayStation 5 Pro , would have the muscle required to offer a 60 FPS mode . However, Rockstar confirmed to Kotaku that even the PS5 Pro is "not powerful enough" to handle the game's simulation at higher framerates.
 While the PS5 Pro features a significantly upgraded graphics processor (GPU), its central processor (CPU) is only marginally better than the base PS5 . Because GTA 6's dense world simulation relies heavily on the CPU, the hardware simply creates a bottleneck.
 "While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates," explained Marc Chambers, Technology Production Director at Rockstar.
 Instead of a framerate boost, Rockstar is utilizing the PS5 Pro's extra power to push the game's visual fidelity to its absolute limits. While the base PS5 and Xbox Series X rely on ray-traced reflections and global illumination, the PS5 Pro version adds ray-traced shadows and uses PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) for a sharper, cleaner image.
 Will a 60 FPS mode come in a future update?
 Rockstar has not confirmed any plans to release a 60 FPS patch for the PS5 or Xbox Series X|S in the future . Given the fundamental CPU limitations of the current console generation, it is highly unlikely that a performance mode will be added post-launch.
 Players who desperately want to experience GTA 6 at 60 FPS or higher will likely have to wait for the eventual, though currently unannounced, PC port or a future next-generation console release.
